what_it_does: Studies how temperature changes affect the reliability of ferroelectric memory (a type of storage that uses polarization switching in hafnium zirconium oxide materials) when stacked vertically in 3D neural network accelerators. As the chip heats up during computation, the electrical properties of the memory cells change, affecting their ability to store data reliably. The work characterizes this behavior and proposes dynamic optimization of write voltages to compensate for temperature-induced changes, improving reliability in hot spots.
